description: Registered suppressions. Every live suppression directive (oxlint, eslint, ts-expect-error, ts-ignore, ts-nocheck) must match an entry by file and directive, and every entry needs a live suppression. An entry names its scope, reason, native alternatives examined, owner, versions and retirement trigger.

exceptions.reason: The launcher opens the user's default browser, and the command differs per operating system (open, xdg-open, cmd /c start). Bun and Node expose the operating system only as the ambient process.platform, which the Effect diagnostics (effect/no-cross-runtime, effect/no-ambient-authority) reject outside the Effect environment. HostPlatform is the one adapter that reads it and hands it on as a service.
nativeAlternativesExamined: A platform service in effect 4.1.0: none exists. Its own persistence/UserDirectories module reads process.platform inside its implementation, so the installed Effect has no public capability for it.
@effect/platform-bun 4.1.0 BunServices (ChildProcessSpawner, FileSystem, Path, Terminal, Stdio): none reports the operating system.
Path.sep to tell Windows from the rest: cannot tell macOS from Linux, and trying open before xdg-open is unsafe (on some Linux systems open is openvt).
Config.string over an environment variable (OS is set on Windows only): not available on macOS or Linux.
A compile-time constant per cross-compiled target (bun build --define): leaves the development entry (bun src/dev.ts) without a value, and adds a second source for a fact the runtime already knows.
exceptions.retirementTrigger: An Effect release exposes the host operating system as a service (or an Effect platform layer reports it), or the launcher stops choosing a command per operating system.
